stories.headline: JD Vance says Haley Stevens' endorsement of GOP's Mike Rogers will 'certainly' help Michigan Senate race
stories.note: Stevens' crossover gives Rogers cover with voters who'd normally never pick a Republican, Vance says.
body: Vice President JD Vance told reporters at Joint Base Andrews on Monday that Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens' endorsement of Republican Mike Rogers will help Rogers in Michigan's Senate race against Democrat Abdul El-Sayed.

Vance had just come back from two rallies for GOP candidates in Ohio and New York. He argued the endorsement could give some voters who don't usually back Republicans "permission" to vote for Rogers, and he praised Rogers as a patriot while calling El-Sayed a "crazy person."
Stevens announced her backing of Rogers on Sunday after El-Sayed's campaign told her to stay away from his events. She said she doesn't belong in his campaign.

Both candidates wrote Election Eve opinion pieces for Fox News Digital. El-Sayed said he's held more than 700 events across 120-plus cities, while Rogers, a former Army officer and FBI agent, went after El-Sayed's ties to far-left streamer Hasan Piker. Stevens has also criticized that connection.

Why it matters: A sitting Democratic congresswoman vouching for the Republican, with the vice president amplifying it, gives Rogers a late boost in one of the Senate races that could decide control of the chamber.

stories.headline: House Dems demand Haley Stevens' exile as Jeffries reveals deadline on deciding her fate
stories.note: Democrats are fighting each other over Stevens on the eve of the vote instead of closing ranks.
body: House Democrats are split over how to punish Rep. Haley Stevens of Michigan after she endorsed Republican Mike Rogers over Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed on Nov. 1. Leaders say they'll wait until after the election to decide.

Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said Stevens "made a terrible decision" and "blindsided everyone," and promised a discussion about next steps when members return. Reps. Delia Ramirez and Pramila Jayapal have already called for her removal from the caucus.

Michigan's Democratic Party chairman, Curtis Hertel, said Stevens is no longer a member of the state party and won't be in the future. Rep. Debbie Dingell said Stevens had told her several times over the weekend that she wouldn't endorse Rogers.

Stevens, who lost the Senate primary to El-Sayed and leaves Congress at year's end, had a rocky relationship with his campaign. It broke down after his team asked her not to show up at his events. Even her communications director's auto-reply said he left her office on Nov. 1, the day she backed Rogers.

Why it matters: Democrats are spending the last hours before Election Day attacking one of their own, which keeps the spotlight on El-Sayed's weaknesses and hands Republicans a story about a party at war with itself.

stories.headline: Union boss stuns with major Republican endorsement as election nears
stories.note: Teamsters chief Sean O'Brien voted for GOP Sen. Ashley Moody, a blow to the Democrats' union base.
body: Teamsters General President Sean O'Brien, who leads a union of about 1.3 million members, announced Sunday that he voted in Florida for Republican Sen. Ashley Moody.

O'Brien credited Moody with working alongside the Teamsters to protect pensions, defend good-paying jobs and back union apprenticeship programs. He said the union wants to work with her on the Senate HELP Committee to pass the Faster Labor Contracts Act.

A self-described "lifelong Democrat," O'Brien also spoke at the 2024 Republican convention after saying Democrats ignored his request to speak at theirs. Moody said she was proud to have his support and would keep fighting for working families.

Moody's Democratic opponent, state Rep. Angie Nixon of Jacksonville, whose platform is seen as DSA-aligned, answered by giving a shout-out to rank-and-file Teamsters voting for her. Some online critics called O'Brien a "scab" and knocked him for voting in Florida.

Why it matters: Organized labor has long been a Democratic pillar, and the head of one of the country's biggest unions publicly backing a Republican senator is more evidence that working-class voters are up for grabs.

stories.headline: Battleground Dem touts bipartisan record, but can't name single issue she'd work with Trump on
stories.note: Minnesota's Peggy Flanagan talked up her bipartisan record but couldn't name one issue she'd work on with Trump.
body: Minnesota Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan, the Democrats' Senate nominee, was asked by Fox News' Bill Melugin on Sunday whether there's any policy she could work on with President Trump. She talked about her bipartisan record in the state Legislature and at the Children's Defense Fund, but didn't name one.
Instead, Flanagan said she's "deeply concerned" about what she called the administration's "continued grift," and said voters want a check on Trump and a rollback of cuts that hurt Minnesota.
Her campaign has called for dismantling ICE, passing Medicare for All and reversing the administration's Medicaid and SNAP cuts.

She faces Republican Michele Tafoya, a former NFL sideline reporter who has made the race about the fraud scandal under Gov. Tim Walz, Flanagan's boss. The race has tightened enough that Fox News moved it from "Likely Democrat" to "Lean Democrat." Trump has urged voters to back Tafoya, who calls herself a pro-choice Republican.
Why it matters: Minnesota is a rare chance for Republicans to flip a blue Senate seat, and a Democrat who can't name any common ground with the president undercuts her own moderate pitch.

stories.headline: Talarico campaigns alongside Democrat who called ICE 'new KKK' and demanded its abolition
stories.note: Talarico praised a House candidate who called ICE the 'new KKK,' handing Texas Republicans an easy immigration contrast.
body: Texas Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico shared the stage Thursday with Frederick Haynes III, a Dallas pastor running for the House seat Jasmine Crockett is leaving. At the get-out-the-vote stop, Talarico called Haynes "your next congressman" and thanked him for his remarks.
In his speech, Haynes accused Trump of turning ICE into "the new KKK" and said it's time to abolish the agency.

Haynes has a record of seeing politics through race. He called Charlie Kirk's views "rooted in White supremacy" in 2025, though he later condemned Kirk's killing and political violence, and he has strongly supported reparations. Talarico has also backed reparations, calling them part of his faith tradition.

Talarico hasn't formally endorsed Haynes, and his campaign didn't respond when asked whether the praise means he supports Haynes' views. Talarico has pitched himself as a moderate who can still be exciting.
Why it matters: Talarico needs Republican-leaning Texans to see him as a moderate, and appearing with an abolish-ICE candidate makes that a lot harder in the race's final days.

stories.headline: EXCLUSIVE: Woman allegedly raped by illegal alien after Clinton-appointed federal judge ordered his release
stories.note: ICE says a Honduran man a federal judge freed in August went on to rape a Minnesota woman, strengthening the GOP's case on enforcement.
body: Federal immigration officials told Fox News that Marcotulio Melendez Diaz, 42, from Honduras, has been charged with raping a woman inside her Mounds View, Minnesota, home on Oct. 11 while he was working there as a handyman. Officials said her indoor surveillance camera recorded the assault.

According to ICE sources, Melendez Diaz was caught and released at the border under the Biden administration in April 2024, then arrested again in Minnesota in January 2026 during Operation Metro Surge.

An immigration judge ordered him deported in March, and he appealed. While that appeal was pending, U.S. District Judge Orlando Garcia, a Clinton appointee in Texas, granted his habeas petition and ordered him freed, finding his detention unlawful or too long.

His appeal was rejected Oct. 9, making the deportation order final. Two days later, he was charged with first-degree criminal sexual penetration. He's in custody and could face up to 30 years. ICE said the crime "could have been PREVENTED."
Why it matters: The case gives Republicans a vivid example of how court-ordered releases can let dangerous illegal immigrants back into communities, on the day Americans go to the polls.

stories.headline: Pentagon's top spies tasked with 'no-fail' mission as Hegseth puts foreign midterm meddling in crosshairs
stories.note: Hegseth has every military spy agency on watch for foreign meddling in today's vote.
body: Secretary of War Pete Hegseth issued a September directive ordering the Pentagon's whole intelligence apparatus to treat protecting the 2026 midterms from foreign interference as a "no-fail mission."

The order goes beyond Cyber Command and the NSA to include the Defense Intelligence Agency and the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency. It tells them to use every authorized asset against foreign election threats and has Cyber Command counter foreign cyber activity in coordination with Homeland Security.

The military's role ends at the border. State and local officials run elections, and the FBI and DHS handle the domestic side. The directive doesn't create new powers or a new organization, and the Pentagon hasn't said whether it added staff or resources.

Intelligence officials say they've seen no sign that a foreign adversary has tried to tamper with voting machines or vote counting. They're still tracking influence efforts from Russia, China and Iran, with Russia the most active.
Why it matters: The administration can point to a department-wide push to guard the election's integrity, answering Democratic claims that it isn't serious about election security.
